headline.caveat: up to; unsigned — terms unsettled and the arrangement could still collapse

nature_md: NVIDIA is negotiating a guarantee of up to ~$250B of lease and construction-debt obligations for OpenAI's planned 10GW campus in Piketon, Ohio (a former uranium-enrichment site being developed by SoftBank's energy subsidiary). If OpenAI misses lease or debt-service payments, NVIDIA covers them — letting lenders price the debt against NVIDIA's balance sheet, since OpenAI has no investment-grade rating. The backstop would exclude the chips themselves; NVIDIA is separately discussing financing OpenAI's chip purchases for the site, reported at up to ~$350B. Nothing is signed.

accounting.payer_treatment_md: If signed: a financial guarantee — initially recognized at fair value, with the maximum exposure disclosed but the full $250B not carried as a liability unless payment becomes probable. Largely off-balance-sheet contingent exposure, the same mechanism regulators flagged in Google's TeraWulf/Cipher lease backstops but at ~50x the scale.
accounting.payee_treatment_md: OpenAI would gain access to investment-grade-priced lease/construction debt it could not raise on its own credit. The leases/debt would sit with the project owner (SoftBank-side development entities) and OpenAI as lessee — keeping the campus itself off OpenAI's balance sheet while creating enormous fixed payment obligations.

both_sides_md: **Bear:** a $250B guarantee 'proves the debt markets said no' (TechTimes framing) — the vendor standing behind its customer's debt is the purest form of the Lucent/Nortel vendor-financing pattern, and if OpenAI stumbles NVIDIA absorbs losses vastly exceeding any equity check. **Bull:** a guarantee is not a cash outlay; it locks NVIDIA in as effectively exclusive compute supplier to the largest planned AI campus for a decade, and NVIDIA only pays if OpenAI — which had ~$25B ARR in early 2026 and is heading to IPO — actually defaults.

events.title: WSJ/CNBC report NVIDIA in talks for up-to-$250B OpenAI backstop
events.why_it_matters: Moves NVIDIA from equity investor to potential guarantor of customer debt — a categorical escalation of circularity risk.
